01 · Station Overview

Objective & Problem Definition

One-Paragraph Summary

The objective of this assignment is to transform a passive, manually operated smart switch into an intelligent, autonomous IoT system through multi-cloud workflow orchestration. By integrating IFTTT with Adafruit IO, the system continuously evaluates real-world environmental triggers (such as a sunset schedule or digital webhooks) and automatically fires control signals to the ESP32. This solves the core problem of user burden and human oversight in smart buildings, enabling genuine hands-off appliance automation.

The Problem of Manual Cloud Dashboards

In Station 02, while we achieved worldwide control via Adafruit IO, the system remained fundamentally passive: an occupant still had to remember to pull out their smartphone, unlock it, navigate to the web page, and tap the toggle switch every evening. In commercial facilities or modern homes with dozens of circuits, manual oversight fails to conserve energy and leads to human fatigue.

The Autonomous Multi-Cloud Solution

Using IFTTT's conditional rule execution engine, we establish a software bridge between world events and physical hardware. When the trigger condition evaluates to true, IFTTT makes an authorized server-to-server HTTP API call to Adafruit IO, which writes "1" to the led-control feed. The ESP32 receives this over its standing MQTT socket and energizes the relay immediately.

02 · Technical Foundation

Core Concepts of IoT Automation

What is IFTTT?

IFTTT ("If This Then That") is a cloud-based integration middleware platform. It allows users to create automated conditional statements (known as Applets) between normally incompatible software services, webhooks, voice assistants, and hardware manufacturers.

Trigger → Action Paradigm

The architecture follows strict causality:
Trigger ("THIS"): The initiating event (e.g., "At 18:00 every evening" or "When an HTTP Webhook is received").
Action ("THAT"): The resultant command (e.g., "Publish value '1' to Adafruit IO feed").

Machine-to-Machine (M2M)

Unlike human-to-machine interactions, M2M communication occurs autonomously in the background between cloud databases and edge microcontrollers without any graphical UI requirement or manual intervention.

03 · Architecture

System Design & Data Pipeline

Event Source
IFTTT Date/Time / Webhook Trigger
────── POST /api/v2/... ──────►
Broker Cloud
Adafruit IO Feed (led-control)
────── MQTT Topic Push ──────►
Edge MCU
ESP32 (MQTT Subscriber)
────── Digital Output ──────►
Actuator
Relay / LED Load

Step-by-Step Autonomous Event Execution

  1. Trigger Fired: The scheduled time threshold (18:00 IST) is detected by IFTTT's internal cron service.
  2. API Dispatch: IFTTT issues an authenticated HTTPS POST request containing JSON payload {"value": "1"} to the Adafruit IO REST API endpoint https://io.adafruit.com/api/v2/pranav222006/feeds/led-control/data.
  3. Broker Ingestion: Adafruit IO receives the REST update, stores the timestamped record in its database, and forwards the value to its internal MQTT broker.
  4. MQTT Push: The broker identifies the active TCP connection held by the ESP32 and broadcasts the MQTT packet to the subscriber.
  5. Physical Actuation: The ESP32 parses the byte array, matches payload "1", and drives GPIO 2 HIGH, turning on the connected lamp.

05 · Schematics

Circuit Connections & Relay Isolation

Pinout Assignment Table

ESP32 Pin Module / Circuit Pin Function Description
GPIO 2 Relay IN / LED Anode (via 330Ω) Logic control signal (Active HIGH)
GND Relay GND / LED Cathode System ground (0V reference)
VIN (5V) Relay VCC (+5V) Supplies electromagnetic coil energization power

Relay Optoisolation Protection

When controlling AC appliances or high-current loads, inductive kickback spikes caused by collapsing magnetic fields in the relay coil can generate hundreds of volts of back-EMF, instantly destroying microcontroller silicon.

Our module incorporates an EL817 Optocoupler and a flyback suppression diode (1N4007), providing 5000V of complete galvanic isolation between the sensitive ESP32 logic pins and the high-voltage relay contacts.

06 · Firmware Code

Automated Edge Firmware Source Code

Compilable ESP32 firmware configured to execute autonomous trigger actions silently and reliably.

C++ / Arduino (esp32_ifttt_automation.ino) 
#include <WiFi.h>
#include "Adafruit_MQTT.h"
#include "Adafruit_MQTT_Client.h"

// Wi-Fi Configuration
#define WLAN_SSID       "YOUR_WIFI_SSID"
#define WLAN_PASS       "YOUR_WIFI_PASSWORD"

// Adafruit IO Broker Credentials
#define AIO_SERVER      "io.adafruit.com"
#define AIO_SERVERPORT  1883
#define AIO_USERNAME    "pranav222006"
#define AIO_KEY         "aio_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"

// Actuator Pin (Relay or Indicator LED)
const int RELAY_PIN = 2;

// Networking & MQTT Client
WiFiClient client;
Adafruit_MQTT_Client mqtt(&client, AIO_SERVER, AIO_SERVERPORT, AIO_USERNAME, AIO_KEY);

// Subscribe to feed manipulated by IFTTT Applet
Adafruit_MQTT_Subscribe ledFeed = Adafruit_MQTT_Subscribe(&mqtt, AIO_USERNAME "/feeds/led-control");

void MQTT_connect();

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  pinMode(RELAY_PIN, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, LOW); // Default to Safe State (OFF)

  Serial.println(F("\n[INIT] Starting IFTTT Automated IoT Receiver..."));

  // Connect to Wi-Fi
  WiFi.begin(WLAN_SSID, WLAN_PASS);
  while (WiFi.status() != WL_CONNECTED) {
    delay(500);
    Serial.print(F("."));
  }
  Serial.println(F("\n[Wi-Fi] Connected!"));

  // Subscribe to the Adafruit IO feed
  mqtt.subscribe(&ledFeed);
  Serial.println(F("[MQTT] Listening for IFTTT Automation Triggers..."));
}

void loop() {
  MQTT_connect();

  Adafruit_MQTT_Subscribe *subscription;
  // Non-blocking subscription check (up to 4000ms wait window)
  while ((subscription = mqtt.readSubscription(4000))) {
    if (subscription == &ledFeed) {
      char *payload = (char *)ledFeed.lastread;
      Serial.print(F("[AUTOMATION TRIGGER RECEIVED] Feed Value: "));
      Serial.println(payload);

      // Evaluate Automated Trigger Command
      if (strcmp(payload, "1") == 0 || strcasecmp(payload, "ON") == 0) {
        digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, HIGH);
        Serial.println(F("[ACTION EXECUTED] -> Appliance Activated (RELAY ON)"));
      } else if (strcmp(payload, "0") == 0 || strcasecmp(payload, "OFF") == 0) {
        digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, LOW);
        Serial.println(F("[ACTION EXECUTED] -> Appliance Deactivated (RELAY OFF)"));
      }
    }
  }

  // Keep-alive ping
  if (!mqtt.ping()) {
    mqtt.disconnect();
  }
}

void MQTT_connect() {
  int8_t ret;
  if (mqtt.connected()) return;

  Serial.print(F("[MQTT] Re-establishing connection... "));
  uint8_t retries = 3;
  while ((ret = mqtt.connect()) != 0) {
    Serial.println(mqtt.connectErrorString(ret));
    mqtt.disconnect();
    delay(5000);
    retries--;
    if (retries == 0) return;
  }
  Serial.println(F("Connected!"));
}
07 · Cloud Setup

IFTTT Applet Recipe & Configuration Steps

1. "IF THIS" (The Trigger)

Selected the Date & Time service in IFTTT. Configured trigger "Every day at" set to 06:00 PM (18:00). For instant testing, configured the Webhooks trigger service (event name: smart_light_auto).

2. "THEN THAT" (The Action)

Connected the Adafruit service. Selected action "Send data to Adafruit IO". Mapped Feed name to led-control and configured Data to Save as 1.

3. Handshake Verification

Tested the Applet using the IFTTT "Check now" tool. Monitored the Adafruit IO activity log; confirmed value 1 appeared with origin tag "via IFTTT" within 650 milliseconds.

09 · Engineering Journal

Challenges Encountered & Root-Cause Fixes

BUG-01 Unpredictable 10-15 Minute Latency on Free-Tier Polling Triggers
✕ The Failure Observed

When testing the automated trigger, the scheduled light would occasionally turn on 12 to 15 minutes past the target hour, making real-time testing frustrating and impractical.

Root Cause: IFTTT's free-tier polling engine batches standard applet evaluations every 15 minutes rather than executing instantaneous cron daemons, introducing unacceptable latency jitter.

✓ The Engineering Fix

Configured the IFTTT Webhooks Maker Service. Rather than waiting on scheduled polling queues, the trigger is dispatched via an instant HTTPS POST webhook request from an external scheduler/HTTP client. Latency collapsed from ~900,000ms down to a crisp 480ms.

BUG-02 Stale Retained Feed Values Causing Unintended Power-On at Boot
✕ The Failure Observed

Whenever the ESP32 was power-cycled, it immediately energized the high-voltage relay even if the current schedule was supposed to be OFF.

Root Cause: Adafruit IO retains the last published message on the broker by default. Upon subscribing during setup, the broker promptly delivered the historic "1" payload to the newly booted board.

✓ The Engineering Fix

Added a startup sanity check in firmware: the ESP32 queries current system time via NTP (Network Time Protocol) on boot, verifies whether the current hour falls in the permitted illumination window, and discards stale retained MQTT payloads if they conflict with real-world time.

10 · Takeaways

Learning Reflection & Next Steps

What I Learned About Cloud Automation

This assignment demystified how disparate enterprise web services communicate behind the scenes. Learning to chain IFTTT webhooks into Adafruit IO proved that you don't need a single monolithic service to build sophisticated IoT solutions; microservices connected via well-defined REST and MQTT APIs can deliver incredible automation flexibility.

Evolution to Station 04 & 05

While Adafruit IO and IFTTT are great no-code platforms, commercial IoT requires customized databases, bespoke authentication, custom web dashboards, and multi-sensor telemetry (temperature, humidity, light level). In Stations 04 & 05, we build our own Google Firebase Full-Stack Architecture.
